fullName: Coherent Surface Scattering Imaging beamline: station 9-ID-D and the 9-ID-GT 'Grand Tube'

status2026.detail: Operations of the old 9-ID (USAXS, Bionanoprobe) were suspended on 2022-08-01 and the old enclosures were removed by 2022-12-22 (9-ID home page; 9-ID news). The Grand Tube was unloaded in four sections in August 2023 and installed in Sep-Oct 2023 (APS-U pictures 2023; APS-U update Sep 2023; 9-ID news). The user manual says 'Since first light in 2024-2, 9-ID operates with a single revolver undulator' (9-ID source slide). That date must refer to the source/front end, because X-rays could not enter 9-ID-A before its shielding verification on 2024-12-18. Shielding verification: 9-ID-A and 9-ID-MH on 2024-12-18, 9-ID-D and 9-ID-GT (Grand Tube) on 2025-01-28..30 (9-ID news; 9-ID home page). Technical commissioning began 2025-02-03; 9-ID 'transitioned to full operations' on 2026-03-14; run 2026-2 (from 2026-05-27) gave 50% of beamtime through the Beamtime Allocation Committee and run 2026-3 (from 2026-09-09) gives 80% of beamtime to General User Proposals for GI-SAXS/WAXS/XPCS and CSSI (9-ID home page). The Beamline Directory lists 9-ID-D as 'Operational/Accepting General Users', on-site access (Beamline Directory). Still incomplete vs the 2019 design: only the downstream undulator slot is filled (upstream empty, 9-ID source slide, APS ID table 2026); no liquid-surface diffractometer or multilayer monochromator appears in the as-built component lists (9-ID user manual).

tagline: X-rays skim chips and films like skipping stones; a 20-metre vacuum tube catches the sparkle that reveals their nanoscale structure.
plainSummary: Many modern technologies live in layers thinner than a soap bubble: computer chips, solar-cell films, battery coatings, flexible plastic electronics. Looking inside them is hard, because they sit on thick supports that block a beam shone straight through. CSSI instead skims an extremely pure, laser-like X-ray beam across the surface at a fraction of a degree, like skipping a stone on a pond. The film scatters a tiny share of the X-rays into a grainy 'speckle' pattern, a fingerprint of every bump and buried edge. To read it, the camera must be far away so each speckle spreads over many pixels. So the beamline ends in the Grand Tube: a steel vacuum tube 20 metres long and nearly 3 metres wide, with an 18-megapixel camera riding inside on a carriage. Computers work backwards from the speckle to a 3D picture, and watching the speckle twinkle shows how films flow, wrinkle or self-organise, from thousandths of a second to many minutes. The upgraded APS makes this practical: its beam is about 100 times more coherent.
expertSummary: 9-ID is a single, non-canted ID beamline (revolver U21/U25, 2.35 m, downstream slot of a dual-inline straight; upstream slot empty) behind a windowless HHL front end. All beam-steering optics upstream of the KB deflect horizontally (the public sources do not state why; keeping vibrations out of the vertical plane is the usual reason): two horizontally deflecting mirrors (MR-1 flat, MR-2 bendable; Pt/Si/Cr stripes) and an LN2-cooled horizontally deflecting DCM in 9-ID-A, followed by a zoom focusing system: CRL-1 transfocator in the 9-ID-MH mini-hutch (~43 m), CRL-2 (~51 m) and a bendable KB pair (V then H; Pt-coated in the FDR; ~54 m, ~650 mm working distance, 0.5 µm diffraction-limited target, 14-19 nrad angular stability; sample stability 55 nrad per SPIE 2025) in 9-ID-D. Tunable 6-25 keV; spots from ~0.5 to ~30 µm. Station 9-ID-D hosts the CSSI solid-sample station (z = 54.992 m; vertical sample surface, horizontal scattering plane, 5-axis flexure nanopositioning with interferometric/capacitive metrology), a high-load hexapod for GI-XPCS, and the GIXS diffractometer migrated from 8-ID-E (z = 56.590 m; horizontal samples, in-air Pilatus 1M-F for GIWAXS). Downstream, the 9-ID-GT 'Grand Tube' (2.75 m × 20.5 m, 8 mm stainless steel, pink-beam-rated) carries an in-vacuum EIGER 16M and an MM-PAD on a 3-axis carriage at 2.9-21.8 m from the CSSI sample, giving speckle oversampling with 75-150 µm pixels and q-space tiling. Techniques: CSSI (phase retrieval with DWBA/multislice/holographic forward models, rotation series), GI-XPCS (1 ms-1000 s), GISAXS/GIWAXS with operando environments.

whatAPSUEnables.plain: CSSI only works with very orderly ('coherent') X-rays, whose waves march in step. The old APS beam was mostly disorderly: in a 2012 test it took a few hours to record one usable pattern from a specially made, oversized gold test pattern. The upgraded APS beam is about a hundred times more coherent, so realistic samples can be measured quickly enough to follow them as they change, For movies of the speckle 'twinkling' the gain is larger still: for the same picture quality the fastest change you can catch improves with the square of the brightness, so in principle changes up to about 10,000 times faster become measurable. In practice the camera sets the limit, at about a thousandth of a second.
whatAPSUEnables.expert: The MBA lattice (41.5 pm natural emittance; zero-current ID source ~12-15 µm × 3-8 µm rms, SR parameters 2024) raises the coherent fraction at 10 keV from ~0.05% (pre-upgrade, σx ~275 µm) to ~2.6% (round-beam mode) or ~6% (flat-beam mode), i.e. ~50-130×, and the horizontal coherence length at 30 m from ~2 µm to ~40-50 µm (derived here from the 2024 storage-ring parameters, single-electron photon terms for a 2.35 m device). Peak brilliance of the U21/U25 revolver is ~1-2 × 10²² ph/s/mm²/mrad²/0.1%BW near 9-11 keV. That is 'two orders of magnitude' above the pre-upgrade Undulator A; the 9-ID source slide shows ~10²⁰ for the old U33, i.e. ~100-200×. The same slide's coherent-fraction curve (~6% at 10 keV, ~2% at 25 keV vs ~0.05% / ~0.015% for the old APS) matches the flat-beam derivation here. For XPCS, SNR = β·I·√(TτN) grows linearly with intensity (brilliance), so at fixed SNR and total time the shortest accessible correlation time falls as 1/brilliance², ~10⁴× shorter for ~100×. In practice the detector frame rate (~1-2.5 ms) is the limit. Coherence-preserving horizontal-deflection optics, nano-focusing (to ~0.5 µm) and a 20 m in-vacuum flight path with 75-150 µm-pixel detectors let the speckle be oversampled even at 25 keV, while 3D detector translation extends q-coverage to nm-scale resolution.
quantitative: Coherent fraction at 10 keV: ~0.05% pre-upgrade (σx 275 µm, σy 10 µm) vs ~2.6% (round mode) / ~6% (flat mode) for the 2.35 m revolver on APS-U (derived here from the 2024 storage-ring source parameters; formula λ/4π per plane)
Horizontal coherence length at 30 m, 10 keV: ~2 µm pre-upgrade vs ~48 µm (round) / ~41 µm (flat) on APS-U; vertical ~58 µm vs ~70-160 µm (derived, ξ = λ z / (2π Σ); SR parameters 2024)

Peak brilliance of the U21/U25 revolver >10²² ph/s/mrad²/mm²/0.1%BW at 10 keV, 'two orders of magnitude higher than the current Undulator A' (PDR 2017; also the 9-ID source-characteristics slide); the 9-ID slide shows U21 1st harmonic ~2 × 10²² near 10-11 keV vs ~1.1 × 10²⁰ peak for the old APS U33 (9-ID source slide)
Pre-upgrade APS delivered 0.01%-0.1% coherent photons over the hard X-ray range (PDR 2017)
2012 CSSI demonstration at 8-ID-E: ~10⁹ coherent ph/s, 7.35 keV, sample-detector 0.7 m, a few hours per pattern, max 3000 counts; resolutions 2.6 µm × 22 nm × 2.7 nm (PDR 2017; Sun et al. 2012)

Design flux at 9-ID with KB focusing at 8.8 keV: 9.2 × 10¹³ ph/s/0.1%BW into 0.75 × 0.42 µm (3 × 2 coherent modes); CRL-2: 9.4 × 10¹³ into 3.5 × 1.7 µm; CRL-1 full beam: 3.4 × 10¹⁴ into 29 × 16 µm (FDR 2019, Table 4.58). Directory quotes ~1.2 × 10¹³ ph/s for the KB mode (Beamline Directory)

XPCS: at fixed SNR the shortest accessible time scales as 1/brilliance² (the 9-ID source slide words it 'scales as (Brilliance)²', meaning the improvement factor) → ~10⁴ shorter for a ~100× brilliance gain; GI-XPCS at 9-ID targets 10⁻³ to 10³ s (Beamline Directory; Strzalka 2025)
Sample-to-detector distance 2.9-21.8 m in vacuum (APS CSSI page) vs 0.7 m in the 2012 demonstration (PDR 2017)
9-ID source slide: coherent fraction ~6% at 10 keV and ~2% at 25 keV (APS-U, U25/U21) vs ~5 × 10⁻⁴ and ~1.4 × 10⁻⁴ (APS, U33), i.e. ~100-150× (read from plot)

PDR (2017) promised 'two to three orders of magnitude increase in coherent flux'; it assumed a 4.8 m undulator length. As built there is one 2.35 m device, so ~100-200× is the realistic gain (PDR 2017; 9-ID source slide; APS ID table 2026)

techniques.name: Coherent Surface Scattering Imaging
techniques.plain: A lens-free way of taking 3D pictures of tiny structures sitting on a surface. The X-ray beam grazes the surface; the scattered light forms a speckle pattern that a computer turns back into an image, like reconstructing an object from the sparkle it makes.
techniques.expert: Coherent diffractive imaging in grazing-incidence reflection geometry near the critical angle (αi ~0.1-1°). Ewald-sphere intersection gives sensitivity to qz; oversampled speckle (λ D / (p d) ≥ 2) recorded without a beamstop on a high-dynamic-range detector. Reconstruction must handle dynamical (multibeam) scattering: DWBA with four reflection/transmission paths, finite-element DWBA, multislice forward models with autodiff, and nonuniform-FFT iterative phasing of rotation series (in-plane φ rotation of a few degrees fills the poorly resolved beam-direction axis). 2012 demo (8-ID-E, 7.35 keV, CCD at 0.7 m): 2.6 µm × 22 nm × 2.7 nm resolution (along-beam x in-plane x surface-normal). Later work with more flux and better detectors (APS 8-ID, PETRA III P10) pushed in-plane resolution below 5 nm, and ptychographic CSSI has reconstructed extended patterns.

techniques.name: Grazing-Incidence X-ray Photon Correlation Spectroscopy
techniques.plain: Instead of a still picture, watch how the speckle pattern twinkles. Fast twinkling means the surface is moving fast. This measures how thin films flow, roughen or rearrange without touching them.
techniques.expert: Intensity autocorrelation g₂(q,τ) = <I(t)I(t+τ)>/<I>² of the speckle in GISAXS geometry, evanescent-wave depth selection below/above αc; relaxation rates Γ(q) distinguish diffusion (q²), overdamped capillary waves (Γ = γ q/(2 η) for thick films) and ballistic/jamming dynamics (q¹). At 9-ID: in-vacuum EIGER 16M at 3-20 m, 1 ms-1000 s, high-load hexapod sample stage; GPU correlation with boost-corr in automated DM workflows.

techniques.name: Grazing-Incidence Small-Angle X-ray Scattering
techniques.plain: Measures the average size, spacing and shape of nanoscale features (pores, grains, stripes) across a whole film.
techniques.expert: Ensemble-averaged nanostructure (1-100s nm) of supported films via DWBA analysis (GIXSGUI, GIXS-U), with in situ thermal/solvent-vapour annealing, spin-coating and deposition; EIGER 16M in the Grand Tube provides long camera lengths.

techniques.name: Grazing-Incidence Wide-Angle X-ray Scattering
techniques.plain: Shows how molecules or atoms are stacked and which way crystals point in a thin film, for example in solar cells or plastic electronics.
techniques.expert: Molecular/crystal packing and texture of thin films via an in-air Pilatus 1M-F (135 fps) on the WAXS detector motion system 9ID-BI-7 next to the GIXS diffractometer; operando electrochemistry, Linkam HFSX350-GI stage (−180 to 300 °C per directory), UR3e sample robot.

techniques.name: Grazing-incidence multibeam X-ray holography (Lloyd's-mirror surface holography)
techniques.plain: The flat substrate acts as a mirror: light scattered by the sample interferes with its own reflection, creating a hologram that encodes the height of features, sometimes from a single snapshot.
techniques.expert: Interference between the scattered wave from a 3D surface pattern and its substrate-reflected copy near the horizon (αf < ~0.3°) gives dark-field, low-noise holographic fringes with period ~2π/(2d) in qz for a scatterer at height d; analysed with FE-DWBA (more than 5 million cells) and a first-principles holographic propagation model to recover 3D form factors at nm/sub-nm resolution from a single view.

scienceCases.title: Seeing buried nanocircuits in 3D without cutting the chip
scienceCases.plain: Chip makers need to check the exact shape and height of tiny wires and layers, but slicing a chip to look inside destroys it. CSSI reads the 3D shape from X-rays bouncing off the surface, so the wafer stays intact.
scienceCases.expert: Substrate-supported, non-periodic patterns cannot be measured in transmission CDI or ptychography without thinning. CSSI and reflective holography give critical-dimension (CD) and height metrology of planar patterns on thick substrates; the 2012 proof of principle reconstructed a lithographic Au 'Argonne' pattern with 22 nm in-plane and ~2.7 nm normal resolution, and later APS/P10 data reached better than 5 nm in-plane. The 2023 first-experiments workshop included a NIST talk, 'Metrology for Semiconductor Industry' (R. J. Kline).

scienceCases.title: 3D shape from a single snapshot: an X-ray Lloyd's mirror
scienceCases.plain: A famous 19th-century optics trick uses a mirror to make light interfere with its own reflection. At grazing angles the silicon substrate plays the mirror, and the resulting hologram reveals the height of a pattern from just one image.
scienceCases.expert: Chu et al. (2023) showed that multibeam scattering near total external reflection makes a single grazing-incidence view sensitive to 3D structure; FE-DWBA (more than 5 million cells) reproduces the data and a first-principles holographic model recovers stacked Au-bar thicknesses with nm/sub-nm precision (single Au bar at PETRA III P10: 8.0 keV, 1.7 × 3.5 µm CRL focus, EIGER X 4M at 5.0 m, incidence 0.2-0.8°, 0.5-1 × 10¹¹ coherent ph/s; stacked bars at APS 8-ID-I: 7.35 keV, 2.2 × 2.5 µm, Lambda 2M at 3.95 m, ~5 × 10⁹ coherent ph/s, incidence 0.6°). This single-view mode is aimed at irreversible, in situ/operando processes at 9-ID.

scienceCases.title: Teaching computers to invert surface speckle (physics-informed reconstruction)
scienceCases.plain: Ordinary 'undo the Fourier transform' tricks fail near a mirror-like surface. New algorithms simulate the X-rays slice by slice and adjust a 3D model until the simulated speckle matches the measurement.
scienceCases.expert: Multislice forward model with PyTorch autodiff reconstructs elongated 3D patterns from single CSSI frames (8-ID prototype, 7.36 keV, ~2 × 2 µm beam, flux 5 × 10⁹ ph/s; simulations assume 100× more flux as at APS-U); a 2026 nonuniform-FFT iterative phasing framework derives sampling requirements and reconstructs isolated 3D objects from rotation series at as few as one or two incident angles.

scienceCases.title: Plastic electronics that breathe while they work
scienceCases.plain: Soft 'mixed conductor' polymers used in bio-sensors swell and shrink as ions flow in and out. Watching how grazing X-ray speckles flicker while the device is switched on and off shows the material's inner structure straining and slowly rearranging.
scienceCases.expert: Operando grazing-incidence XPCS of an acid-treated PEDOT:PSS film in an electrochemical 'cone cell' (RbBr or NaCl electrolyte) was measured at pre-upgrade APS 8-ID-I: 10.92 keV, 2 × 20 µm beam, 10 Hz frames. Speckle dynamics tracked internal strain and mesoscale reorganisation during doping and de-doping, revealing structural hysteresis and a slow non-equilibrium process on re-doping (Wu et al., Nat. Mater. 2024, with 9-ID staff co-authors Strzalka, Narayanan and Zhang; complementary operando GIWAXS came from earlier work). At 9-ID the same studies combine GIWAXS on the former 8-ID-E instrument with GI-XPCS on the coherent APS-U beam over 10⁻³ to 10³ s.

scienceCases.title: Watching solar-cell films crystallise as they are spun
scienceCases.plain: Perovskite solar films form in seconds as a liquid is spun on a disc. X-rays show which chemical route the crystals take, and how to steer them to a stable, efficient film.
scienceCases.expert: In situ GIWAXS during spin coating of mixed 2D/3D halide perovskites revealed competing 'solvate' and 'orientation' formation mechanisms set by the precursor stoichiometry (Hoffman et al., Chem 2022; measured during 5-min spin-coating runs at APS 8-ID-E, the GIXS instrument that has since moved to 9-ID, per the APS highlight). '3D morphology of photovoltaic thin films' is one of the six prime CSSI research areas in the FDR; 9-ID supports spin coating, thermal and solvent-vapour annealing, and user solar simulators.

scienceCases.title: How thin films flow, roughen and self-organise
scienceCases.plain: Even a solid-looking plastic film has a restless surface with tiny waves. Speckle 'twinkling' measures how fast those waves relax, and how patterns grow when films are made or etched.
scienceCases.expert: GI-XPCS of ultrathin molten polystyrene films showed that the capillary-wave model must include a shear modulus (viscoelastic effects) (Jiang et al., PRL 2007), and coherent GISAXS follows self-organised ion-beam nanopatterning and thin-film growth (e.g. de Gennes narrowing, Myint et al., PRL 2021, measured at NSLS-II CHX). FDR science drivers include self-assembly at surfaces/interfaces, capillary instability in confined geometry and GI-XPCS of interfacial dynamics.

scienceCases.title: At-wavelength metrology of coherence-preserving X-ray mirrors
scienceCases.plain: Super-smooth X-ray mirrors must be flat to a fraction of a nanometre. CSSI can test them with the very X-rays they will reflect.
scienceCases.expert: Listed as a CSSI prime research area (FDR 4-8.1/4-8.6.1); the KB mirrors themselves need <0.3 nm (H) and <0.2 nm (V) rms figure error to keep focal broadening below 3%. 9-ID-D also carries a compact wavefront sensor (9ID-BD-6, APS Optics design) downstream of the CSSI station.

keyParameters.value: 6-25 keV, fully tunable
keyParameters.note: FDR design 6-30 keV (FDR 2019); source slide says continuous tunability 8-25 keV (9-ID source slide); U25 first harmonic reaches down to ~4.6-5 keV, so 6 keV is set by optics/operations.

keyParameters.note: Feature page labels it 'Working distance 2.9 to 21.8 m' without naming the reference sample (assumed CSSI) (APS CSSI page); 3-20 m for GISAXS/GI-XPCS (Strzalka 2025); design 'up to 23 m' (MEDSI 2020); '>20 m' (SPIE 2025).

keyParameters.value: ~20.5 m long, 2.75 m diameter stainless-steel vacuum vessel, 8 mm wall, pink-beam rated
keyParameters.note: 20 m × 2.75 m (Struct. Dyn. 2025); '66-foot-long, ~nine feet in diameter' (APS CSSI page); '70-foot-long enclosure', 100,000 lb (APS News 2023); '20 m long, 3 m diameter' (APS-U news 2023); '20 meters long and three meters wide' (APS-U update, Sep 2023). 20.5 m / 2.75 m / 8 mm is from the 2020 shielding design study (Sunil 2020).

keyParameters.label: Detectors
keyParameters.value: In-vacuum EIGER 16M (400 fps, 550 fps burst); in-vacuum MM-PAD; in-air Pilatus 1M-F (135 fps)

MM-PAD: 150 µm pixels, mixed-mode high dynamic range; PDR lists 256 × 384 px and a 47 × 49 mm area, which disagree with each other (256 × 384 × 150 µm = 38.4 × 57.6 mm) (PDR 2017).

insertionDevices.name: Revolver undulator APS21R25#5 - U21 array (APS21#10)
insertionDevices.type: planar hybrid permanent-magnet revolver undulator (two magnet arrays on a rotating carriage)
insertionDevices.notes: 112 periods (length derived 112 × 21 mm = 2.35 m; slide says 2.3 m); device min gap 8.5 mm, admin min 8.72 mm, user min 9.0 mm; Keff 1.38 / E1 8.34 keV at 8.5 mm; Ptot 5.4 kW, Pdens 216 kW/mrad² at 200 mA. Used for the high-flux 8.8 keV fundamental and its 3rd harmonic (26.4 keV) in the FDR design. Installed in the DOWNSTREAM slot (FDR: centre ~1.25 m downstream of the straight-section centre). The 9-ID source slide calls it a 'Tandem revolver undulator – 2.3 m long (21 and 25 mm periods)' with 'continuous tunability over 8-25 keV' (9-ID source slide). ID table footnote: effective periods = N – 2 (APS ID table 2026). Estimated E1 at the 9.0 mm user minimum gap is ~8.9-9.0 keV, so the FDR's 8.8 keV U21 fundamental (K = 1.305) is just below reach on the U21 fundamental; the U25 array covers it.

insertionDevices.name: Revolver undulator APS21R25#5 - U25 array (APS25#8)
insertionDevices.type: planar hybrid permanent-magnet revolver undulator (second array of the same device)
insertionDevices.notes: 94 periods; Keff 1.99 / E1 4.58 keV at 8.5 mm; Ptot 8.1 kW, Pdens 225 kW/mrad². Rotated into place instead of U21 to cover lower fundamentals; 1st and 3rd harmonics of the two arrays together cover 6-25(30) keV (PDR 2017; 9-ID source slide).

insertionDevices.name: Upstream slot (planned planar U21, not installed)
insertionDevices.notes: FDR Table 3.13: '09-ID dual inline: upstream Planar 2.1, downstream Rev 2.5/2.1, phase shifter/corrector'; FDR Table 4.56 used both devices (4.6 m) for flux estimates. As of Sep 2026 the upstream position is empty and 'capable of hosting a second undulator in the future' (9-ID source slide; APS ID table 2026).

source.canting: None. 9-ID is a dual-inline (non-canted) straight with a single device installed downstream; beam leaves along the straight axis.
source.frontEnd: APS-U High Heat Load Front End (HHLFE; limits 21 kW total, 590 kW/mrad²): permanent-magnet clearing magnet, LPPS, storage-ring valve, burn-through fixed mask BTFM1, FM2, collimator, GRID XBPM1, FM3, photon shutter PS2 with intensity monitor IM1, safety shutters SS1/SS2, wall collimator through the ratchet wall, then on the exit table in 9-ID-A: exit mask (2 × 2 mm, with XBPM2) at 25.4 m and tungsten exit collimator (5 × 5 mm) at 26.1 m. 9-ID uses the windowless exit with a built-in differential pump (FDR ch. 3 Table 3.1, Sec. 3-2.1; FDR 2019 4-8.3). FDR design power through the 2 × 2 mm mask: 2.10 kW for U21 with two devices (K 1.305), 0.812 kW for U25 (K 1.939) (FDR 2019 Table 4.56).
source.sourceSizeAndDivergence: Electron beam at an ID straight (SR parameters 2024, Aug 2024; values are for ZERO current; intrabeam scattering at 200 mA enlarges them somewhat): round-beam mode σx = 12.3 µm, σy = 8.26 µm, σx′ = 2.34 µrad, σy′ = 3.47 µrad (28.7 pm each plane); flat-beam mode (κ = 0.1) 14.5 / 3.08 µm and 2.75 / 1.29 µrad. Single-electron photon terms for L = 2.35 m (derived, σr = √(2λL)/4π, σr′ = √(λ/2L)): 1.9 µm / 5.1 µrad at 10 keV, 1.2 µm / 3.2 µrad at 25 keV – the photon divergence dominates, so the photon source is ~12.5 × 8.5 µm rms and ~5.6 × 6.2 µrad rms at 10 keV (round mode). PDR quoted APS-U ranges σx 5-30 µm, σy 2-14 µm vs 275 / 10 µm pre-upgrade (PDR 2017 Table 6.18).

branches.name: 9-ID single line (pink or monochromatic)
branches.description: One beam path; no canting or branching. In monochromatic mode the HDCM displaces the beam horizontally: at 42.38 m the mono beam runs ~10 mm outboard of the pink-beam path (XBPM drawing), and masks in 9-ID-A/MH (dual-aperture PM-5, pink beamstop BS-2) handle both paths. Three sample positions share the line inside 9-ID-D: CSSI solid-sample station (54.992 m), hexapod for GI-XPCS (~55.9 m) and GIXS diffractometer (56.590 m); all share the Grand Tube detectors downstream.

components.name: Empty upstream undulator slot
components.distanceNote: approx: mirror image of the downstream device position (+1.25 m, FDR Table 4.56); not given explicitly. Drawn as an empty outline.
components.plain: An empty parking space for a second undulator. Half of this straight section of the electron ring is left free, so another magnet array can be added later to make the X-ray beam brighter still.
components.expert: FDR baseline placed a planar U21 here (dual-inline straight with phase shifter/corrector between devices, FDR Table 3.13); the 2026 ID table lists no device in S09 US and the 9-ID manual says the slot can host a second undulator in the future.

components.name: Revolver undulator U21/U25 (APS21R25#5)
components.distanceNote: FDR Table 4.56: revolver centre 1.25 m downstream of the centre of the straight section (distance convention: from straight-section centre)
components.plain: The light source: rows of strong magnets above and below the electron beam make the electrons slalom and shine an intense, narrow X-ray beam. It is a 'revolver': it carries two sets of magnets, one repeating every 21 mm and one every 25 mm, and swaps in whichever gives the most light at the chosen X-ray colour.
components.expert: Hybrid PM revolver: U21 array (112 periods, Keff 1.38, E1 8.34 keV at 8.5 mm; 5.4 kW, 216 kW/mrad²) and U25 array (94 periods, Keff 1.99, E1 4.58 keV; 8.1 kW, 225 kW/mrad²), user min gap 9.0 mm. 1st and 3rd harmonics cover 6-25 keV; brilliance ~10²² near 10 keV. Only device in the straight since first light (run 2024-2).

components.name: High-heat-load front end (windowless, in the tunnel)
components.distanceNote: approx: front end occupies roughly 14-23 m inside the tunnel; 19.4 m is the documented XBPM1/upstream-mask position for APS-U front ends (FDR Table 3.9, CUFE) – HHLFE element positions for 9-ID are not published
components.plain: The gatekeeper inside the concrete shielding: water-cooled masks, beam monitors and safety shutters that tame a beam carrying several kilowatts and can stop it in an instant. Its exit has no window: even a thin one could blemish the orderly beam CSSI depends on.
components.expert: HHLFE (21 kW, 590 kW/mrad² limits): clearing magnet, LPPS, SRV, BTFM1, FM2, collimator, GRID XBPM1, FM3, PS2/IM1, safety shutters SS1/SS2, wall collimator, FEV. Windowless configuration with built-in differential pumping for 9-ID.

components.name: Ratchet shield wall (with wall collimator)
components.distanceNote: approx: ~22.1-23.6 m by analogy with the 28-ID ray-trace plan used in the CHEX dossier; not documented for 9-ID
components.plain: The thick concrete wall between the accelerator tunnel and the experiment hall. The X-rays leave the tunnel through a small, heavily shielded opening.
components.expert: Front-end wall collimator sits in the ratchet-wall penetration; FDR Fig. 4.51 shows 9-ID-A starting at ~23.5-24 m.

components.name: Front-end exit mask (2 × 2 mm, with XBPM2)
components.distanceNote: exact: FDR Table 4.57
components.plain: A water-cooled metal block with a 2 mm square hole. It lets only the bright, orderly core of the beam into the beamline and soaks up the rest as heat.
components.expert: Standard HHL exit mask, 2 (H) × 2 (V) mm, integrated XBPM2; differential pump instead of a Be window (windowless exit).

components.name: Front-end exit collimator (tungsten, 5 × 5 mm)
components.distanceNote: exact: FDR Table 4.57
components.plain: A tungsten block with a 5 mm hole. It stops stray, very-high-energy radiation from the accelerator (bremsstrahlung) from travelling along with the X-rays.
components.expert: Tungsten exit collimator, 5 × 5 mm aperture (narrowed for small-offset monochromators, FDR 3-2.1.1).

components.name: Slits SL-1 (white beam, 9ID-SL-1)
components.distanceNote: exact per FDR Table 4.57 (HHL white-beam slits w/ tungsten edge inserts); as-built label 'Slits, PB 9ID-SL-1'
components.plain: Four movable, tungsten-edged jaws that trim the raw beam to about a millimetre square, so the first mirror receives only the part it can use.
components.expert: High-heat-load white/pink-beam slits with W edges defining the mirror acceptance (~1 × 1 mm, FDR M1 acceptance 0.96 × 1.0 mm²).

components.name: Mirror MR-1 (flat, horizontal deflection; 9ID-MR-1)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (9-ID user manual, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m
components.plain: The first optic: an ultra-smooth mirror struck at an extremely shallow, glancing angle, far less than a degree. It bounces the useful X-rays sideways while very-high-energy X-rays and much of the heat carry straight on. Like all the beam-steering optics upstream of the final focusing mirrors, it deflects sideways rather than up, a choice many coherence beamlines make to keep the beam steady.
components.expert: First optic; flat, horizontally deflecting, water-cooled (FDR: notched substrate to cut thermal bump by ~10×). As-built coating stripes selected by vertical translation: Pt, Si ('Si stripe for 8 keV'), Cr ('Cr for 11 keV') plus a fourth (manual: 4 stripes). FDR design: 2.4 mrad, Si/Pd/Pt; 474 W incident, 311 W absorbed, 0.82 W/mm² at 8.8 keV (two-device source).

components.name: Secondary collimator SC-1 (9ID-SC-1)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (9-ID user manual, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m (FDR 29.1 m)
components.plain: A heavy-metal block with a small opening that catches radiation scattered off the first mirror, so it cannot travel on down the beamline.
components.expert: Bremsstrahlung/secondary collimator downstream of MR-1.

components.name: Beam flag BD-1 (diamond screen; 9ID-BD-1)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (9-ID user manual, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m (FDR 29.5 m)
components.plain: A diamond screen that can be lowered into the beam. It glows where the X-rays hit, and a camera watches it so the staff can see the beam's position and shape.
components.expert: Diamond screen imaged by camera, 16.13 µm/pixel (calibrated 2024-11-23); shows direct beam when MR-1 is retracted.

components.name: White-beam stop PM-1 (9ID-PM-1)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (9-ID user manual, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m
components.plain: A cooled absorber that catches the part of the raw beam that passes the first mirror without being reflected, so only the reflected beam continues.
components.expert: Manual: 'Photon Mask, WB Stop, 9ID-PM-1' – absorbs the unreflected white beam passing MR-1 (the FDR placed its WB stop 9ID-PM-1 at 33.8 m, after the mono). The as-built layout labels it 'Photon Mask, PB, 9ID-PM-1'; the manual list calls it 'Photon Mask, WB Stop, 9ID-PM-1'.

components.name: Movable photon mask PM-2 ('DAMM'; 9ID-PM-2)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (9-ID user manual, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m
components.plain: A movable mask (labelled 'DAMM' on the drawings) that can be positioned to block or pass selected parts of the beam, protecting the equipment downstream.
components.expert: Movable pink-beam photon mask labelled 'DAMM' in the as-built layout (manual lists a movable pinhole mask); acronym expansion not documented. The shielding analysis assumed a pinhole-defined source plus two mirrors. The manual component list (ELOG 897) writes it as 'Pinhole Mask, Moveable, 9ID-PM-1', an evident numbering slip. The layout drawing labels it 'DAMM: Photon Mask, movable, PB, 9ID-PM-2'.

components.name: Secondary collimator SC-2 (9ID-SC-2)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (9-ID user manual, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m
components.plain: Another heavy-metal collimator, catching stray scattered radiation ahead of the second mirror.
components.expert: Secondary collimator ahead of MR-2.

components.name: Mirror MR-2 (bendable, horizontal deflection; 9ID-MR-2)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (9-ID user manual, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m
components.plain: A second glancing mirror that bounces the beam back parallel to its original path. It can be gently bent to adjust how the beam converges, and its extra reflection strips out more of the unwanted high-energy X-rays, one reason the steel Grand Tube can serve as its own radiation shield.
components.expert: Not in the FDR (one mirror). Horizontally deflecting bender with the same 4-stripe layout as MR-1 (operated on Cr in the logged configuration). The two-mirror geometry gives extra harmonic rejection and keeps the line-of-sight blocked. It matches the assumption of the 2020 shielding design study for the pink-beam-rated Grand Tube: pinhole-defined source and two mirrors at ≥ 3.0 mrad. Whether the as-built angles meet 3.0 mrad is not published.

specs.coating stripes: same 4 stripes as MR-1 (logged on Cr)

components.name: Photon mask PM-3 (9ID-PM-3)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (9-ID user manual, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m
components.plain: A cooled mask that absorbs stray beam after the second mirror, protecting the hardware downstream.
components.expert: Pink-beam photon mask.

components.name: Beam flag BD-2 (9ID-BD-2)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (9-ID user manual, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m
components.plain: A second glowing screen and camera, used to check the beam after the two mirrors.
components.expert: Diamond screen, WB/PB flag.

components.name: Photon mask PM-4 (9ID-PM-4)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (9-ID user manual, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m
components.plain: A protective mask that trims stray beam just before the monochromator.
components.expert: Pink-beam photon mask upstream of the monochromator.

components.name: Bremsstrahlung collimator BC-1 (9ID-BC-1)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (9-ID user manual, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m (listed in the manual between PM-4 and SL-2; FDR 34.2 m)
components.plain: A dense collimator that blocks high-energy stray radiation (bremsstrahlung) from the accelerator, part of the beamline's radiation-safety chain.
components.expert: Bremsstrahlung collimator.

components.name: Slits SL-2 (pink beam, 9ID-SL-2)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (9-ID user manual, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m (FDR 29.9 m: moved downstream because a second mirror was added)
components.plain: Adjustable slits that trim the mirror-filtered 'pink' beam to the size the monochromator needs.
components.expert: H+V pink-beam slits.

components.name: Monochromator HDCM (horizontal double-crystal, LN2-cooled; 9ID-MN-1)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (9-ID user manual, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m (FDR 30.65 m)
components.plain: Two perfect silicon crystals, chilled with liquid nitrogen, pick a single X-ray colour (energy) out of the rainbow. Like the mirrors, they bounce the beam sideways rather than up, so the single-colour beam leaves about 10 mm to the side of the pink beam's path.
components.expert: Horizontally deflecting DCM (APS seminar abstract, Strzalka 2025); LN2 cooling and fixed exit per FDR. FDR: Si(111) pseudo channel-cut, 13.0° at 8.8 keV, 163 W absorbed, footprint 4.65 × 1.08 mm. Contains flag 'Flag3 9ID-BD-3' (10 mm diamond region inboard + CdWO4 region outboard, viewed at 45°, 20.833 µm/px; ELOG 906 attachment). The same tag 9ID-BD-3 is also used for XBPM-1 in 9-ID-MH (ELOG 898/909), so the manual has a naming clash. Mono beam exits ~10 mm outboard of the pink path (XBPM drawing at 42.38 m); FDR design had a ~2 mm offset. Vendor appears to be IDT ('IDT Mono', manual).

components.name: Dual-aperture mask PM-5 (9ID-PM-5)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): position estimated by scaling the as-built 9-ID-A isometric layout (9-ID user manual, ELOG 897) between FDR anchors SL-1 = 27.1 m and the FOE downstream wall ~36.9 m; MR-1 then falls at 28.2 m vs FDR 28.25 m
components.plain: A mask with two holes: one for the pink beam's path and one for the single-colour beam, which runs about 10 mm to the side.
components.expert: Dual-aperture pink-beam mask passing both pink and mono beam positions.

components.name: Shielded transport pipe (9-ID-A to 9-ID-MH)
components.distanceNote: approx: between FOE wall (~36.9 m, FDR Fig. 4.51) and the mini-hutch (~41.5 m)
components.plain: A shielded vacuum pipe on stands that carries the beam across the open hall floor from the optics enclosure to the mini-hutch.
components.expert: Shielded transport with support stands (~2 m spacing in FDR Fig. 4.51).

components.name: Pink-beam stop BS-2 (with gate valve GV-5; 9ID-BS-2)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-MH layout and component list (9-ID user manual, ELOG 898), anchored to the surveyed XBPM 9ID-BD-3 at 42.38 m (XBPM drawing)
components.plain: A beam stop that blocks the multi-colour pink beam whenever only the single-colour beam, running 10 mm beside it, is wanted downstream.
components.expert: Pink-beam stop at the upstream end of the mini-hutch; the mono beam passes ~10 mm outboard.

components.name: Beam-position monitor XBPM-1 (Sydor; 9ID-BD-3)
components.distanceNote: exact: 42.380 m on the XBPM drawing; survey 2024-12-03 gave Z = 42.4186 m (XBPM drawing)
components.plain: A sensor that continuously reports exactly where the beam is, so drifts can be spotted and corrected. It is centred between the pink and single-colour beam paths, 10 mm apart.
components.expert: Sydor XBPM (SI-103770), ±13 mm X, ±5 mm Y travel; centred on the midplane between pink and mono beams (10 mm apart); 22 mm bypass aperture. Note: the 9-ID-A layout and ELOG 906 also call the mono flag 'Flag3 9ID-BD-3', so the BD-3 tag appears twice in the manual.

components.name: Slits SL-3 (pink beam, 9ID-SL-3)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-MH layout and component list (9-ID user manual, ELOG 898), anchored to the surveyed XBPM 9ID-BD-3 at 42.38 m (XBPM drawing)
components.plain: Slits that trim stray light from the edges of the beam before it reaches the first set of lenses.
components.expert: Pink-beam slits (same mechanics as SL-4/SL-5).

components.name: Photon shutter PH-1 (9ID-PH-1)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-MH layout and component list (9-ID user manual, ELOG 898), anchored to the surveyed XBPM 9ID-BD-3 at 42.38 m (XBPM drawing)
components.plain: A shutter that can block the X-ray beam inside the mini-hutch. Together with the second shutter at the hutch exit, it lets the beam be stopped before the experiment station.
components.expert: Photon shutter (as-built label 'Photon Shutter, 9ID-PH-1'), upstream of CRL-1 in the mini-hutch. Its safety role (protecting entry to 9-ID-D) is inferred from the name and position, not documented.

components.name: Transfocator CRL-1 (9 lens cartridges; 9ID-RL-1)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-MH layout and component list (9-ID user manual, ELOG 898), anchored to the surveyed XBPM 9ID-BD-3 at 42.38 m (XBPM drawing); FDR placed CRL-1 at 32.4 m in the FOE
components.plain: A 'transfocator': nine cartridges of tiny curved X-ray lenses that slide in or out of the beam on command. It gently focuses the X-rays, the first stage of a zoom lens that ends with the KB mirrors.
components.expert: 9 cassettes, all 2D parabolic: N = 1,1,1,1,1,1,2,4,8 with R = 2000,1000,500,300,200,100,100,100,100 µm (9ID CRL final design review). Provides the larger GIXS/GI-XPCS spots and prefocus for the zoom with CRL-2/KB. FDR version had 12 stacks incl. 1D lenses.

components.name: Beam flag BD-4 (9ID-BD-4)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-MH layout and component list (9-ID user manual, ELOG 898), anchored to the surveyed XBPM 9ID-BD-3 at 42.38 m (XBPM drawing)
components.plain: A screen and camera to check the beam after the first lens stage.
components.expert: PB/MB flag.

components.name: Shutter SH-1 (9ID-SH-1)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-MH layout and component list (9-ID user manual, ELOG 898), anchored to the surveyed XBPM 9ID-BD-3 at 42.38 m (XBPM drawing) (FDR: pink shutter at 35.5 m)
components.plain: A second shutter at the exit of the mini-hutch that can stop the beam before it enters the experiment station.
components.expert: Station shutter (FDR 'Shutter, Pink, 9ID-SH-1').

components.name: Fast shutter (9ID-BI-8)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-D layout and component list (9-ID user manual, ELOG 895), anchored to XBPM 9ID-BD-5 at 53.43 m (XBPM drawing) and the CSSI station at 54.992 m (9-ID user manual, ELOG 916) (FDR slits at 47.7 m)
components.plain: A quick shutter that opens only while the camera is recording, so delicate films receive no more X-rays than needed.
components.expert: Fast experimental shutter on the upstream optical table, synchronised with detector exposures (softGlue timing).

components.name: Attenuator AT-1 (filter foils; 9ID-AT-1)
components.distanceNote: approx: FDR filters at 48.2 m; as-built on the same table as the fast shutter (9-ID user manual)
components.plain: A set of thin metal foils that can be dropped into the beam to dim it when it is too strong for the sample or the camera.
components.expert: Pink/mono-beam filter attenuator.

components.name: Slits SL-4 (9ID-SL-4)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-D layout and component list (9-ID user manual, ELOG 895), anchored to XBPM 9ID-BD-5 at 53.43 m (XBPM drawing) and the CSSI station at 54.992 m (9-ID user manual, ELOG 916)
components.plain: Slits that clean up the beam's edges before the second lens set; closed down further, they pass only a beam narrow enough that its waves stay in step across it.
components.expert: Coherence-defining/cleanup slits upstream of CRL-2 (PDR planned coherence slits ~50 m: 2× vertical, 3× horizontal coherence length).

components.name: Transfocator CRL-2 (10 lens cartridges; 9ID-RL-2)
components.distanceNote: approx: FDR Table 4.57 value; as-built order SL-4 → RL-2 → SL-5 (9-ID user manual)
components.plain: The second, stronger zoom-lens stage: ten lens cartridges that can focus the beam to a spot a few micrometres across, accepting only a few coherent "modes" so the speckle stays crisp.
components.expert: 10 cassettes, all 2D: N = 1,1,1,1,1,1,2,4,8,16, R = 2000-100 µm (cassettes 9 and 10 annotated as swapped). FDR: 3.5 × 1.7 µm (H × V) at 8.8 keV with a 3 × 2-mode coherent aperture, 9.4 × 10¹³ ph/s/0.1%BW.

components.name: Slits SL-5 (9ID-SL-5)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-D layout and component list (9-ID user manual, ELOG 895), anchored to XBPM 9ID-BD-5 at 53.43 m (XBPM drawing) and the CSSI station at 54.992 m (9-ID user manual, ELOG 916)
components.plain: The last slits before the focusing mirrors, trimming away stray light around the beam.
components.expert: Pink-beam slits.

components.name: Beam-position monitor XBPM-2 (Sydor; 9ID-BD-5)
components.distanceNote: exact: 53.432 m on the XBPM drawing; survey 2024-12-03 gave Z = 53.3988 m (XBPM drawing)
components.plain: A second beam-position sensor just before the focusing mirrors, checking that the beam enters them exactly on target.
components.expert: Sydor XBPM, same assembly as BD-3.

components.name: KB focusing mirrors (Kirkpatrick–Baez pair; 9ID-MR-3)
components.distanceNote: approx: FDR has V-KB 1.0 m and H-KB 0.8 m upstream of the 55 m sample (54.0/54.2 m); SPIE 2025 quotes a ~650 mm working distance to the CSSI sample at 54.992 m
components.plain: Two curved mirrors at right angles, one squeezing the beam vertically and one horizontally, focus it to about half a micrometre, some 200 times thinner than a hair. To keep the spot still they must hold their angle to 14–19 billionths of a radian.
components.expert: Two bendable flat mirrors, V upstream of H (FDR: Pt coating, 2.5 mrad; as-built coating and angles not published), piezo-lever weak-link flexure benders, flexure alignment stages with a 4-interferometer metrology frame in UHV chambers on granite air-bearing stages. Targets: 500 nm diffraction-limited focus at ~650 mm WD; angular stability 19 nrad (H) / 14 nrad (V); figure error <0.3 nm (H) / <0.2 nm (V) rms. FDR spots: 0.75 × 0.42 µm at 8.8 keV, 0.66 × 0.35 µm at 26.4 keV. Manual geometry: hexapod centre is 1.818 m from KB-V and 1.552 m from KB-H, so the two mirrors are ~0.27 m apart (9-ID user manual, ELOG 916). The KB and the CSSI sample station sit on one shared granite table.

components.name: Window WN-1 (Be or SiN; 9ID-WN-1)
components.distanceNote: approx (± ~1 m): order from the as-built 9-ID-D layout and component list (9-ID user manual, ELOG 895), anchored to XBPM 9ID-BD-5 at 53.43 m (XBPM drawing) and the CSSI station at 54.992 m (9-ID user manual, ELOG 916)
components.plain: A paper-thin window that X-rays pass through easily, separating the ultra-clean vacuum of the mirrors from the sample chamber.
components.expert: Be or SiN window between KB (UHV) and the CSSI sample chamber (high vacuum).

components.name: CSSI sample station (solid samples, in vacuum; 9ID-BI-2)
components.distanceNote: exact: 'CSSI-SSS: 54992' mm (9-ID user manual, ELOG 916)
components.plain: The heart of CSSI: a vacuum chamber where the sample stands on its edge, like a book on a shelf, while the X-rays graze its surface at a fraction of a degree. Nanometre-precise stages hold that angle steady and turn the sample a few degrees to view it from several directions for a 3D picture.
components.expert: High-vacuum sample chamber; vertical sample surface reflecting in the horizontal plane. 5 DOF (3 linear + pitch about vertical axis + yaw about surface normal) with custom weak-link flexure stages (cm travel, nm MIM; piezo 1 mm stage; pitch correction <1°, tens-of-nrad MIM), three metrology frames (capacitive + laser interferometers; nm linear, 10s nrad angular). Requirement: 50 nrad sample angular stability (MEDSI 2020) / 55 nrad (SPIE 2025). The KB and the sample station share one granite table to cut floor noise and relative motion. High-precision commercial rotation stages give pitch (vertical axis) and yaw (horizontal axis). Three metrology frames: two measure parasitic motion of the rotation stages, one measures the flexure stages. Designed, assembled and installed at 9-ID (SPIE 2025).

components.name: Wavefront sensor (9ID-BD-6)

geometryNotes: Single, non-canted ID line (dual-inline straight, only the downstream revolver installed; source point ~+1.25 m from the straight centre; all distances here are from the straight-section centre as in the FDR tables). Everything sits on the main experiment-hall floor (no LOM or long-beamline building): 9-ID-A FOE (~23.6-36.9 m, wedge-shaped in plan per FDR Fig. 4.51), shielded transport, the small 9-ID-MH mini-hutch (~41.5-45 m, as-built addition), shielded transport, the 9-ID-D station (~47-57.5 m) and the free-standing Grand Tube 9-ID-GT (~57.5-78 m) that is its own pink-beam-rated shielding: a light-grey 2.75 m-diameter cylinder of ~4 flanged sections with stiffener rings and a dished downstream head, resting on saddles on the floor, outside any hutch (APS photo, APS CSSI page). The line ends close to the hall's outer wall (~90 m available). Optics: all upstream deflections are horizontal. MR-1 (flat) and MR-2 (bender) form a horizontal offset pair (~2.9 m apart in the layout). The HDCM deflects horizontally (mono beam ~10 mm outboard of the pink path at 42.4 m; masks PM-5 and XBPM have dual apertures/bypass). The surveyed XBPM bodies at 42.42 m and 53.40 m sit at almost the same horizontal offset from the white-beam axis (X = -8.79 / -8.64 mm), so the downstream beam runs parallel to the original axis, displaced sideways (XBPM drawing). The KB pair (V then H) is the exception: the V mirror deflects the beam vertically (FDR 2.5 mrad grazing, i.e. ~5 mrad upward or downward, direction not documented) and the H mirror horizontally, focusing ~0.65 m downstream. Beam height ~1.4 m above floor throughout (FDR). Inside 9-ID-D (as-built isometric, 9-ID user manual): upstream optical table (fast shutter, attenuator) → slits SL-4 → CRL-2 transfocator stand → slits SL-5 + XBPM-2 table → KB UHV chamber on granite → window → round multi-port CSSI sample chamber on granite → stationary granite with hexapod → GIXS diffractometer on translating granite with in-air Pilatus WAXS detector arm → Grand Tube entrance flange in the downstream wall. Two sample geometries: CSSI sample surface VERTICAL (incidence and specular reflection in the horizontal plane, so the reflected beam and exit-angle axis spread sideways in the tube); GIXS samples HORIZONTAL (classic GISAXS, exit angles vertical). Detector carriage translates along z and in x/y within the 2.75 m bore. Exact as-built z positions are public only for the CSSI station (54.992 m), GIXS (56.590 m) and the two XBPMs (42.38 m, 53.43 m); other positions are estimates (±1 m). Mirror-deflection sense (inboard vs outboard) of MR-1/MR-2 is not documented; only the mono-vs-pink offset direction is. 3D model: true distances along the beam; the real lateral offsets of the mirror pair (~17 mm for two ~3 mrad reflections 2.9 m apart) and of the HDCM (~10 mm) are below hall-scale visibility, so the beam is drawn on one axis. MR-1/MR-2 are drawn as an outboard periscope (sense undocumented). The Grand Tube axis is drawn 0.2 m above beam height so the vessel clears its saddles (axis height unpublished). CSSI is shown with a 0.5° incidence angle (true, but invisible at room scale): the chip faces inboard (side undocumented), so the specular reflection leaves at 1° and lands ~0.35 m inboard of the direct beam 20 m downstream, where the MM-PAD waits; the EIGER 16M sits further inboard at larger exit angles. A floating magnifier above the sample chamber repeats the geometry with the chip enlarged ×8 and the angles exaggerated ×24.

interactiveIdeas.title: Skip a stone with X-rays: the critical angle
interactiveIdeas.concept: A slider tilts a silicon wafer from 0 to 1° in front of an X-ray beam. Below the critical angle the beam reflects almost totally and only a few-nm-deep evanescent wave enters; above it the beam dives in. Show reflectivity curve, penetration depth and the footprint stretching across the wafer.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Why surface X-ray methods work at tiny angles, how depth sensitivity is tuned, and why a 1 µm beam paints a ~0.2 mm stripe on the sample.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: αc = sqrt(2 δ), δ proportional to λ² ρe: Si αc ~0.20° (3.5 mrad) and Au ~0.50° at 8.8 keV, scaling as 1/E. Penetration depth below αc ~ λ/(4π sqrt(αc² – α²)) ~ a few nm (include β for absorption). Footprint = beam size / sin(α): 0.75 µm at 0.2° → ~215 µm. Yoneda peak at αf = αc.

interactiveIdeas.title: Speckle zoom: why the Grand Tube is 20 m long
interactiveIdeas.concept: Drag the EIGER/MM-PAD along the tube (2.9-21.8 m) and sideways; choose energy (6-25 keV) and focal spot (0.6-3.5 µm). The speckle pattern rescales live over a pixel grid; meters show oversampling ratio and the finest resolvable feature.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: The core trade-off of coherent imaging: far away = speckles big enough to sample (oversampling), close or off-axis = higher q = finer detail; the tube allows both by moving the detector in 3D.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Speckle size s ~ λ D / d (d = illuminated size projected normal to the exit direction); oversampling O = s/p ≥ 2 per dimension (Nyquist), ~5 preferred. Examples: 8.8 keV, D = 20 m, d = 0.75 µm → s ~3.8 mm (~50 EIGER pixels); 25 keV, d = 3.5 µm, D = 20 m → s ~0.28 mm (O ~1.9 with 150 µm MM-PAD pixels). Half-period resolution ~ π/q_max, q_max = (4π/λ) sin(theta_max): detector half-width 0.155 m at 20 m and 8.8 keV gives ~9 nm; at 2.9 m ~1.3 nm. In grazing incidence resolution is anisotropic (poor along the beam footprint) – rotation series fix this.

interactiveIdeas.title: Lloyd's mirror in the hard X-ray world
interactiveIdeas.concept: A glowing point (a nanoscale feature) floats above a mirror-like substrate. Move it up and down and watch interference fringes appear on a virtual detector near the horizon, then reverse: given fringes, guess the height.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: How a substrate acts as a built-in reference beam, turning surface scattering into a hologram that encodes height from a single image.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Two paths: direct scattering and scattering reflected by the substrate (phase flip ~π near αf = 0 where Fresnel reflectance → 1). Fringe period in qz ~ 2π/(2d) for height d; strongest for αf < ~0.3° and αi above αc (Chu et al. 2023). Keep Fresnel reflectivity and absorption; it is dark-field (away from specular).

interactiveIdeas.title: Then and now: how orderly is the X-ray beam?
interactiveIdeas.concept: Two virtual pinholes (Young's double slit) at 30 m from the source: toggle between the 1996-2023 APS and APS-U sources and energies. Fringe visibility and the number of 'coherent modes' across the beam change dramatically, especially horizontally.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: What 'coherence' means and why the multi-bend-achromat upgrade made CSSI practical.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Transverse coherence length (rms) ξ = λ z/(2π Σ), Σ = sqrt(σe² + σr²), σr = sqrt(2 λ L)/(4π). At 10 keV, 30 m: APS-U xi_x ~48 µm (round mode), old APS ~2 µm; vertical ~70 µm vs ~58 µm. Coherent fraction per plane = (λ/4π)/(Σ Σ'): ~2.6% (round) / ~6% (flat) total at 10 keV vs ~0.05% before. Use SR parameters 2024 parameters; do not use the 2019 FDR 'brightness mode' as current. SR parameters 2024 values are zero-current; the 9-ID source slide (9-ID source slide) plots ~6% coherent fraction at 10 keV (~2% at 25 keV) for APS-U vs ~0.05% for the old APS, consistent with the flat-beam case. Show coherent FLUX (brilliance × (λ/2)²), not total flux, as the quantity that rose ~100×.

interactiveIdeas.title: Twinkle, twinkle: build a g₂ curve
interactiveIdeas.concept: A live speckle movie from a thin polymer film; the user chooses temperature (viscosity) and film thickness. A cursor-picked speckle's intensity trace feeds a real-time correlation function g₂(τ).
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: How XPCS turns flicker into a relaxation time and how different motions (diffusion, capillary waves) leave different q-dependences.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: g₂(q,τ) = 1 + β |f(q,τ)|², f = exp(-Γ τ) for simple relaxation; diffusion Γ = D q²; overdamped capillary waves on thick films Γ = γ q/(2 η) (thin films: Γ ~ γ h³ q⁴/(3 η)); β (speckle contrast) < 1 set by coherence and pixel/speckle ratio. Fastest time limited by detector (~2 ms at 400-550 fps) and by photons: SNR ~ β * I * sqrt(T τ N); at fixed SNR the shortest τ scales as 1/brilliance². 9-ID window 10⁻³-10³ s.

interactiveIdeas.title: Zoom lens of beryllium: the transfocators
interactiveIdeas.concept: Toggle the 9 + 10 lens cassettes of CRL-1 and CRL-2 (binary stacks of R = 2000..100 µm lenses) and the KB mirrors to zoom the spot from ~30 µm to ~0.5 µm at the sample; see flux and number of coherent modes accepted.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: How X-ray lenses work (weakly), why many lenses are stacked, and the trade-off between spot size and coherent flux.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Thin-lens focal length f = R/(2 N δ) for paraboloid lenses (Be δ ~4.4 × 10⁻⁶ at 8.8 keV, so N=1, R=100 µm gives f ~11 m), combine stacks with 1/f = sum; imaging 1/p + 1/q = 1/f; spot ~ source size x magnification convolved with diffraction ~λ/(2 NA). Use as-built cassettes (CRL design review), not the FDR 12-stack lists.

funFacts: The Grand Tube weighs about 100,000 lb (~45 t). It was unloaded at Argonne in four crated sections in August 2023, assembled in three weeks and installed at 9-ID in Sep-Oct 2023.
The KB mirrors must hold their angle to 14-19 nanoradians, the angle a 1 cm coin subtends seen from about 500-700 km away (MEDSI 2020, SPIE 2025; comparison derived).

In CSSI the mirror-like reflection can be as bright as the incoming beam while useful speckles are 8-10 orders of magnitude fainter – up to 10¹¹ counts/s per pixel near the critical angle – so a special mixed-mode detector (MM-PAD) replaces the usual beamstop.
It is big enough to walk inside: about 2.75 m (9 ft) across and ~20 m long; entering it requires a formal access procedure.
Its 8 mm stainless-steel wall doubles as radiation shielding, so the tube itself is a certified X-ray enclosure (9-ID-GT) rather than a pipe inside a hutch.

The first CSSI demonstration (2012, APS 8-ID-E) used a CCD only 0.7 m from the sample that detected just ~0.13% of scattered photons. It needed a few hours to record one pattern, peaking at 3,000 counts, from a gold 'Argonne' test pattern 400 µm long, 5 µm wide and 40 nm thick.
At a 1 degree grazing angle, raising the sample by 1 µm slides the beam footprint ~57 µm along the surface; the stage must find the surface to <50 nm.
Before the upgrade the horizontal coherence length 30 m from the source was only ~2 µm at 10 keV; at the upgraded APS it is ~40-50 µm (derived from SR parameters 2024).
9-ID used to host the USAXS instrument (now at 12-ID-E) and the Bionanoprobe (now at 2-ID-D); its GIXS instrument moved in from 8-ID-E.
The holographic analysis echoes Humphrey Lloyd's 19th-century mirror-interference experiment, redone with hard X-rays and a silicon wafer as the mirror.

openQuestions: As-built z positions are public only for the CSSI station (54.992 m), GIXS (56.590 m) and XBPMs (42.38 / 53.43 m); the '09-ID Beamline Component Reference Table' and optics schematic are on access-restricted Box. All other positions here are FDR values or ±1 m estimates from isometric drawings.
Enclosure boundaries of 9-ID-MH (~41.5-45 m) and the 9-ID-D / Grand Tube interface (~57.5 m) are estimates; hutch widths are not published (FDR plan figure appears anisotropically scaled).

Mirror incidence angles as built are not published (FDR: single M1 at 2.4 mrad; shielding analysis assumed two mirrors at ≥3.0 mrad). The fourth mirror stripe is unidentified, and whether MR-1 deflects inboard or outboard is unknown.

HDCM: crystal set (FDR Si(111) only; PDR Si(111)+Si(220); the directory lists a 'High resolution' mode with dE/E = 2.8 × 10⁻⁵, which would fit Si(311)) and the fixed-exit offset (FDR '2 mm offset' vs ~10 mm pink/mono separation at 42.4 m in the XBPM drawing) are unconfirmed. No DMM appears in as-built lists although FDR/PDR reserved one.

CRL-1 moved from the FOE (FDR 32.4 m) to the mini-hutch (~43 m) and the lens sets changed (as-built 9/10 cassettes, all 2D, R ≥ 100 µm vs FDR 12 stacks incl. 1D and R = 50 µm), yet the Beamline Directory still quotes the FDR focal sizes (29 × 16 µm, 3.5 × 1.7 µm); actual as-built spot sizes and fluxes need confirmation.

Directory fluxes (e.g. 3.4 × 10¹³ ph/s CRL-1, 9.4 × 10¹² CRL-2, 1.2 × 10¹³ KB at 8.8 keV; 3.2 × 10¹¹ / 3.7 × 10¹¹ at 25 keV, and '3 µm × 12 µm' for CRL-2 high energy) are inconsistent with FDR Table 4.58 by roughly a bandwidth factor or 10×; treat as indicative.

KB working distance: FDR geometry (V 1.0 m / H 0.8 m upstream of sample), MEDSI 2020 (550 mm) and SPIE 2025 abstract ('about 650 mm', verified) differ; ~650 mm is the most recent. The full SPIE paper (measured stability; the abstract states a 55 nrad sample-stability requirement vs 50 nrad in 2020) was not accessible.

Grand Tube dimensions differ by source: 20 m × 2.75 m (Struct. Dyn. 2025), 20.5 m × 2.75 m (shielding paper), '66-foot, ~nine feet' (feature page), '70-foot' (APS news), '20 m × 3 m' (2023 update). The overall vessel incl. heads is probably ~21 m; inner bore assumed 2.75 m.

Detector specifics: EIGER 16M variant (EIGER2 X vs XE; 400/550 fps suggests XE) and the MM-PAD version, mounting and travel ranges inside the tube are not published; beamstop arrangement for GISAXS/CSSI is undocumented.
The FDR liquid-surface diffractometer (57 m, double-crystal beam tilter for liquid/liquid interfaces) is absent from as-built lists; status (deferred or cancelled) unknown.
Second undulator: the upstream slot is empty; no public schedule for installing the planned planar U21 (FDR flux tables assume both devices, 4.6 m).

Exact first-light date: the manual says only 'first light in 2024-2'. Whether CSSI (vs GIXS/GI-XPCS) is routinely offered to general users or mainly in partner/collaborative mode in 2026-3 is not stated beyond the 80% GUP allocation 'for GI-SAXS/WAXS/XPCS and CSSI'.
No published 9-ID (post-upgrade) CSSI reconstruction or GI-XPCS paper was found as of 2026-10-08; science cases cite pre-upgrade 8-ID/P10 work and the legacy 8-ID-E instrument.

'First light in 2024-2' (manual) predates the 9-ID-A shielding verification (2024-12-18), so it cannot mean X-rays in the hutches. The date the first X-rays reached 9-ID-A or 9-ID-D is not published; technical commissioning began the week of 2025-02-03.
The tag 9ID-BD-3 is used both for the mono flag inside the HDCM (9-ID-A) and for XBPM-1 in 9-ID-MH; ask staff which is correct before labelling hotspots.
Vertical-deflection sense of the KB-V mirror (beam up or down) and as-built KB angles and coating are not published.
